events.title: Oil Surge Weighs On European Markets Despite U.K. GDP Strength
events.description: European equities turned negative Wednesday as crude oil climbed 1.8% to $97.90 per barrel amid stalled U.S.-Iran negotiations. Weak German and French data pressured regional markets, though U.K. stocks gained on stronger-than-expected GDP growth.

events.title: Positive Close For Asian Markets
events.description: Asian stock markets closed on a mostly positive note on Wednesday as the likelihood of a Fed rate hike diminished significantly. Easing bond yields as well as the momentum in tech stocks also bolstered sentiment. However, lingering anxiety ahead of updates to inflation and labor market due from the U.S. on Wednesday morning limited gains.

events.title: Oil Prices, FPI Outflows Trigger Sharp Selloff In Indian Markets
events.description: India's key stock indices Sensex and Nifty50 closed lower Wednesday despite early strength, pressured by elevated oil prices and foreign portfolio investor selling in final trading hour. Brent crude climbed to $97.70/barrel.

events.title: FTSE 100 Edges Higher As Revised GDP Shows Stronger Q2 Growth
events.description: U.K. stocks gained ground Wednesday after the Office for National Statistics revised Q2 GDP growth upward to 0.5% from 0.4%. The FTSE 100 rose 0.15% to 10,652.70, though oil price gains amid Middle East uncertainty limited broader momentum.

events.title: Higher Crude Oil Prices, Weak Economic Data Weigh On French Stocks
events.description:
The French stock market's benchmark index CAC 40 slipped into negative territory on Wednesday, as oil prices climbed higher on supply concerns amid lingering uncertainty about Iran and U.S. reaching a deal to end their conflict anytime soon. 

Data showing an acceleration in French inflation in the month of September weighed as well on sentiment.

events.title: German Stocks Pare Gains As Oil Prices Rebound, DAX Slips
events.description: German stocks retreated after initial morning gains as oil prices rebounded. The DAX fell 0.07% while investors assessed September unemployment and retail sales data ahead of preliminary inflation figures.

events.title: Australian Dollar Falls Following Economic Data
events.description: The Australian dollar weakened against other major currencies in the Asian session on Wednesday, despite the releases of economic data from Australia and China.

events.title: European Markets Seen Rising On Wednesday
events.description: A strong positive sentiment is expected to prevail in European stock markets on Wednesday amidst a sharp decline in Fed rate hike expectations. The decline in crude oil prices, the easing in bond yields and the dollar's retreat are also expected to bolster sentiment. Anxiety ahead of the release of PCE-based inflation readings from the U.S. on Wednesday morning is however expected to limit gains.

events.title: Australian Dollar Falls Against Majors
events.description: The Australian dollar weakened against other major currencies in the Asian session on Wednesday.

events.title: Australia Inflation Rises In August
events.description: Australia's consumer price inflation accelerated in August on higher housing and transport costs, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Wednesday. Consumer price inflation rose to 4.0 percent from 3.5 percent in July. Inflation continues to remain above the central bank target range of 2-3 percent.

events.title: China Private Sector Growth Improves
events.description: China's manufacturing and services sectors expanded at faster rates in September as robust new orders underpinned employment, survey results from S&P Global showed Wednesday. The RatingDog China general manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 52.1 in September from 51.5 in August. The score was seen at 51.7. The index has remained above the 50.0 no-change mark.

events.title: Australian Market Sharply Extends Early Gains In Mid-market
events.description: The Australian market is sharply extending its early gains in mid-market moves on Wednesday after opening in the red, adding to the gains in the previous two sessions, with the benchmark S&P/ASX 200 moving up to near the 8,800 level, despite the negative cues from Wall Street overnight, with gains in gold miners and energy stocks partially offset by weakness in iron ore miner and financial stocks.

events.title: Asian Markets Trade Mostly Higher
events.description: Asian stock markets are trading mostly higher on Wednesday, despite the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight, as tumbling crude oil prices on easing supply concerns as Saudi Arabia restored half of the capacity of its East-West pipeline, allaying fears of global inflation and aggressive interest rate hikes. Asian markets closed mixed on Tuesday.
